title: The factory cannot be deployed from a low-bandwidth connection
description:
A deploy that rebuilds the orchestrator image pulls Go, Node, Bun, uv and mise from upstream - mise alone is 116 MB - into a ~3 GB image. On a low-bandwidth link each large transfer fails partway (curl 56 'Send failure: Broken pipe', curl 18 'partial file') and the build never completes.

Measured 2026-09-21, and the diagnosis is worth keeping because three plausible explanations were wrong:
- NOT the factory image: reproduced in a three-line Dockerfile that only downloads mise.
- NOT BuildKit's bridge: --network=host fails identically.
- NOT builds specifically: plain 'docker run curl' on the same URL fails the same way.
It is the link. Small transfers succeed; large ones drop.

Consequences as it stands:
- An operator on a poor connection cannot ship a change to the orchestrator image AT ALL, which now includes every ticfac change, since prs put the ticfac binaries in it.
- bkj makes it maximally bad: the ticfac pins sit at the top of the staged Dockerfile, so a 15 MB binary change invalidates every layer and re-downloads everything.

Worth considering, roughly in order of value:
1. bkj first. Moving the pins down means a ticfac-only change rebuilds the last layers and downloads nothing. That alone converts the common case from impossible to trivial on a bad link.
2. Make the image's downloads resumable and retried. 'curl -fsSL --retry N --retry-all-errors -C -' would survive a drop instead of failing the layer. This is in the VENDORED Dockerfile, so it belongs upstream in ticks - and it would help every ticks user on a bad connection, not just us.
3. Consider whether the deploy should build the image at all when only the ticfac binaries changed, or whether it can push a layer onto the existing image.

Related: h8u - all of these failures reported exit 0, so a scripted deploy would have called them releases.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy whose only change is the ticfac binaries completes on a low-bandwidth connection, and a dropped transfer during a full image build is retried rather than failing the build
